subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Through which blood vessels does the heart muscle itself receive oxygen?
questions.explain: The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with oxygenated blood.

questions.q: Where does most chemical digestion of food finish?
questions.explain: Enzymes from the pancreas and small intestine complete digestion in the small intestine.

questions.q: Where is bile made?
questions.explain: Bile is produced in the liver and then stored in the gall bladder.

questions.q: Which blood component carries oxygen?
questions.explain: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports oxygen.

questions.q: Which chambers of the heart receive blood returning to the heart?
questions.explain: The atria are the upper chambers that receive blood entering the heart.

questions.q: A scientist measures the reaction time of a person catching a falling ruler. This is testing the speed of a:
questions.explain: Catching a ruler requires the brain to process the stimulus and decide to react, so it tests a conscious response.

questions.q: Which mineral-carrying tissue is also important in supporting the plant?
questions.explain: Lignified xylem vessels help support the plant as well as transporting water.

questions.q: By which process do oxygen and carbon dioxide move across the alveolar wall?
questions.explain: Gases move down their concentration gradients by diffusion across the thin alveolar walls.

questions.q: In a knee-jerk reflex, the effector that produces the response is a:
questions.explain: The effector is the muscle that contracts to produce the response, e.g. the leg muscle making the lower leg kick.

questions.q: A motor neurone carries impulses:
options: From a receptor to the CNS
From the CNS to an effector
questions.explain: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors such as muscles or glands.

questions.q: Which structure protects the relay neurones and passes impulses between the body and the brain?
questions.explain: The spinal cord, part of the CNS, contains relay neurones and carries impulses to and from the brain.

questions.q: Why does transpiration slow down when stomata close at night?
options: Water vapour can no longer escape easily through the closed pores
questions.explain: With stomata closed, water vapour cannot diffuse out, so transpiration slows.

questions.q: When you touch a hot object and pull your hand away before feeling pain, this shows that a reflex:
options: Happens before the brain consciously processes the pain
Is slower than a conscious response
questions.explain: The reflex (handled by the spinal cord) acts before the impulse reaches the conscious brain, so you react before feeling pain.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes phloem from xylem?
options: Phloem is made of dead cells
Phloem is made of living cells
questions.explain: Phloem is composed of living cells, unlike the dead xylem vessels.

questions.q: Why are reflex actions important?
options: They are protective and help prevent injury
questions.explain: Reflexes are fast and protective, for example pulling your hand away from a hot object.

questions.q: Why does emulsifying fat by bile speed up its digestion?
options: Bile chemically digests the fat itself
It increases the surface area of fat for lipase to act on
It absorbs the fat into the blood
questions.explain: Bile breaks large fat droplets into smaller ones, giving lipase a larger surface area to work on.

questions.q: What does haemoglobin combine with to transport oxygen?
questions.explain: Haemoglobin binds oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin in the lungs and releases it in the tissues.

questions.q: How are red blood cells adapted to carry oxygen?
options: They have a nucleus packed with DNA
They can change shape to engulf bacteria
They are biconcave and have no nucleus, giving more room for haemoglobin
questions.explain: Red blood cells lack a nucleus and are biconcave, maximising space and surface area for haemoglobin.

questions.q: Why are xylem vessels strengthened with lignin?
options: To keep them hollow and support the plant
questions.explain: Lignin strengthens xylem vessels, keeping them open and helping support the plant.

questions.q: A cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is this in micrometres (µm)?
Bile is stored in which organ before release into the small intestine?
questions.explain: Bile made in the liver is stored in the gall bladder until needed.

questions.q: In the food test, what colour does Benedict's solution turn when heated with a reducing sugar?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick-red/orange when a reducing sugar is present.
